body:
## Problem

The Windows test suite runs with Bun's default **5000 ms** per-test budget, and `dev`'s own Windows leg carries **12 tests over 4 seconds** on a normal, fully green run.

None of them times out. They do not need to. The margin is under a second, so any additional IO in that job — or any ordinary runner contention — tips one of them over, and which one is a coin flip.

## The measurement

From PR #3291, comparing its Windows leg against `dev`'s Windows leg an hour earlier, **2612 tests matched by name**:

- Median ratio branch/dev: **0.87**. The branch was *faster* overall, 93 s against 149 s. There was no broad slowdown.
- **Exactly one test per run** exceeded the budget, and it was a **different test each run** — 27x and 23x their own normal times.
- Control: **six recent `dev` Windows legs produced zero 5000 ms timeouts. The branch produced one in each of two runs. 0/6 against 2/2.**

The two victims were `captureWorkflowSource > replaces a stale capture rather than merging two vintages` (9625 ms, against 6.20 ms on ubuntu in the same run and 351.86 ms on dev's own Windows leg an hour earlier) and `generate-bundled-defaults: untracked-file guard (#1578) > exits 1 and leaves the bundle untouched for an untracked workflow default` (7995 ms).

Both spawn subprocesses and copy trees inside `%TEMP%`. For the `generate-bundled-defaults` group across 7 shared tests: dev median 355 ms / max 1843 ms; branch run 1 median 548 ms / max 1622 ms; branch run 2 median 485 ms / max **7996 ms**. Slightly slower median, dramatically fatter tail.

## Why this is worth solving

**This is the thing behind most of today's noise.** Seven distinct tests blew the Windows budget on a single day, each on a PR that did not touch the failing package. Six pull requests were red for reasons already fixed on `dev`. Every one of those cost someone a diagnosis, and the cumulative effect is that a red Windows leg stopped carrying information — people learn to shrug, and then a real failure gets shrugged at too.

The individual failures have been chased one at a time all day: #3286, #3287, #3288 and the skips in #3280 are each a symptom of a suite that has no headroom. Fixing them one by one does not change the fact that the next PR to add a little IO tips over a different test.

## Why now

It is measured. Until #3291 ran the comparison above, "Windows is flaky" was a belief; now there is a control (0/6 versus 2/2) and a named cluster with numbers. That will decay — the figures are tied to a particular `dev`, and the tail grows as suites grow.

## Desired outcome

The Windows suite has enough headroom that ordinary contention does not produce a red leg, and a Windows timeout once again means something is wrong.

## Invariants

- **No budget bump.** #2924's standing decision holds: if a test blows the budget, it is spending on something it should not. Raising the ceiling hides the cluster rather than removing it, and would make every future timeout less informative.
- **No Windows skips as the general answer.** One deliberate, recorded exception exists (#3280, for a `tar` child that never exits) and it is not a precedent for the rest.
- Whatever changes, the tests must still assert what they assert today.

## Acceptance

- The 12-over-4-seconds cluster is enumerated with per-test Windows timings, so the list is a fact rather than an estimate.
- For each, either the accidental cost is removed, or it is declared runner-floor residual with its cost attributed — the bar #2924 already sets for a residual.
- A green `dev` Windows leg has meaningful margin on every test, not sub-second on twelve of them.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

The common shape in both observed victims is **subprocess spawn plus tree copy in `%TEMP%`**, which is also #2306's thesis — Windows timeouts cluster on subprocess-spawning tests under `bun --filter --parallel`. That is the place to look first.

`bun run bench:capture` on `dev` (from #3285) profiles the capture path directly and reports per-phase timings and operation counts, which covers one of the two victims. #3282 has the Windows measurement of that path already assigned.

## Links

- #2924 — the Windows budget-edge ledger, and the standing rule against budget bumps and skips
- #2306 — subprocess-spawning tests under `bun --filter --parallel`
- #3282 — Windows capture-cost measurement, harness already on `dev`
- #3287 — the exec-code isolation family, one instance of this cluster
- #3291 — the PR whose measurement produced the numbers above
title: test(ci): the windows suite has no headroom — 12 tests sit within a second of the 5000ms budget
